value.rationale: A rank-reduced covariance forecast is interpreted as uncertainty, so a natural potential assumption is that increasing the rank yields larger variance in every direction when both approximate the same exact PSD covariance. The explicit counterexample proves that this monotonic confidence intuition is false for exact projected continuous dynamics even though each individual prediction is PSD and conservatively below the full covariance. It isolates the rank-dependent rotation mechanism independent of discretization or observation correction, giving a substantive structural boundary for rank adaptivity.
